events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Avery, NC; Burke, NC; Caldwell, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 400 AM EDT.

* At 139 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen over the past 12
hours. Steady rises are occurring in area streams including the
Linville River, Wilson Creek, Johns River, Mulberry Creek and
Warrior Fork Creek. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, B.R. Parkway-Linville Falls To Grandfather,
Linville Falls, B.R. Parkway-Little Switzerland To Linville, Lake
James State Park, Grandfather Mountain State Park, Lake James,
Jonas Ridge and Edgemont.

Wilson Creek at Adako Rd, 3 miles southwest of Colletsville has risen
above flood stage and is still rising. Flooding of low-lying areas
adjacent to Wilson Creek is developing with lesser impacts to
vulnerable property.  More significant floodwaters are beginning to
impact low-lying areas, with inundation approximately 2-4 ft deep.
Low-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2-3 ft of
floodwaters.  Campgrounds, secondary roads, and outbuildings may be
experiencing flooding up to 1-2 ft deep.  Flooding less than 1 ft
deep may begin impacting basements and primary roads.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Northwest Plateau; Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave; Lake Mead - AZ side; Lake Mohave - AZ side; Hualapai Mountains; Northwest Deserts; Death Valley National Park; Western Mojave Desert; Eastern Mojave Desert, Including the Mojave National Preserve; Morongo Basin; Cadiz Basin; San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley; Esmeralda and Central Nye County; Lincoln County; Northeast Clark County; Western Clark and Southern Nye County; Sheep Range; Spring Mountains-Red Rock Canyon; Las Vegas Valley; Southern Clark County; Lake Mead - NV side; Lake Mohave - NV side
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following
areas, Hualapai Mountains, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead -
AZ side, Lake Mohave - AZ side, Northwest Deserts and Northwest
Plateau, southeast California, including the following areas, Cadiz
Basin, Death Valley National Park, Eastern Mojave Desert, Morongo
Basin, San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley and
Western Mojave Desert, and Nevada, including the following areas,
Esmeralda and Central Nye County, Lake Mead - NV side, Lake Mohave
- NV side, Las Vegas Valley, Lincoln County, Northeast Clark
County, Sheep Range, Southern Clark County, Spring Mountains-Red
Rock Canyon and Western Clark and Southern Nye County.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Incoming tropical moisture will lead to widespread shower and
thunderstorm activity, some of which may cause flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
